voice-branch-jargon.notes: No branch/audit working labels, bean ids, PR/branch references, audit-doc pointers, or agent work-narration found in the .md body or the .ts title.

trap-negation-contrast.evidence: No assert-by-denying constructions in the four-sentence preamble.

trap-triples.evidence: Four items, not a padded three, and each names a distinct sub-part.

trap-closing-aphorism.evidence: 'Finally, it outlines ...' is the last roadmap item, not a flourish.

trap-meta-commentary.evidence: no meta-commentary on the block's own rhetoric

All four sentences take the document as subject (This sub-section consolidates / The sequence validates / It empirically verifies / Finally, it outlines). Signposting what a section will do is legitimate in a preamble and is not the narrated-emphasis trap, but the register is uniformly self-referential and a reader gets no content until the sub-section itself.

trap-superlative.evidence: 'It EMPIRICALLY VERIFIES the LP-duality hypothesis class on compound braids.' LP duality is a theorem, not a hypothesis class awaiting empirical verification, and the preamble cites no compute, no witness and no block for the claim. 'strict confinement-NF structural rules' and 'the EXACT NF-structure forcing rules' likewise assert strictness and exactness with nothing behind them at this point in the text.
trap-superlative.notes: PROPOSED: name the block or witness each clause refers to, or soften to what the sub-section actually contains.

trap-nonspeakable.evidence: Two stacked noun chains in four sentences: 'strict confinement-NF structural rules', and 'the exact NF-structure forcing rules required for downstream normal-form evaluations' — nine words of stacked modifiers that abbreviates normal form to NF and then spells it out in the same sentence.
trap-nonspeakable.notes: NOT FIXED INLINE: repairing this requires knowing what 'NF-structure forcing rules' names, which the preamble does not say. PROPOSED: 'the rules that force the normal-form structure, which the downstream evaluations require', and use one spelling of normal form throughout.
